summary.headline: Zuari Industries guides net debt to about INR700 crores by FY26-end, dependent on ~INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows over six months.
summary.overview: Sugar operations delivered record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 101.7% capacity utilisation in FY26, with sugar realisation up to INR4,053/quintal from INR3,894. Standalone PAT turned to INR12 crore from a loss of INR37 crore, and consolidated PAT was INR105 crore versus a loss of INR94.4 crore. Management says the St. Regis Dubai project (98% complete, BCC received 21 May 2026) is the main deleveraging lever, with external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore expected to fall to about INR700 crore by year-end. Ethanol remains under pressure from stagnant prices and roughly 100% industry overcapacity, and the Envien bioethanol JV is still stabilising with OMC tenders delayed.

segments.name: Sugar (SPE division)
segments.commentary: Record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 163.7 lakh quintal for the season; recovery 10.26% (lower YoY); production 14.4 lakh quintal vs 14.7 lakh; sales 14.3 lakh quintal vs 15.1 lakh quintal; realisation INR4,053/quintal vs INR3,894.

segments.name: Ethanol and power
segments.commentary: Ethanol production up 10.1% and sales up 0.7%, realisation INR62.6/litre (up 1.1%). Power sales 857 lakh units vs 907 lakh units, as the mill did not operate in April 2025.

segments.name: Zuari Infraworld (real estate DM)
segments.commentary: Total income up 78% YoY. India DM projects aggregate GDV about INR4,900 crore across Hyderabad, Kolkata (Panihati, Adventz Corporate Center) and Bangalore plotted development. Dubai St. Regis project 100% sold, 50% collected during construction, balance on BCC.

segments.name: Simon India (EPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 income INR29.8 crore vs INR8.9 crore; FY26 income INR89.4 crore vs INR18.8 crore; FY26 EBITDA INR6.8 crore vs INR0.9 crore. About INR95 crore of projects under execution.

segments.name: Financial services
segments.commentary: Zuari Finserv FY26 income INR20.1 crore (up about 4.1%) and EBITDA INR5.6 crore (up about 60%). Zuari Insurance Brokers GWP INR99.4 crore (up about 9%), brokerage income INR10.2 crore (up about 40%).

segments.name: Envien bioethanol JV (ZEBPL)
segments.commentary: Plant commissioned 1 January 2026 and under stabilisation; OMC second and third round tenders have not yet been floated, with existing orders running to October.

guidance_outlook: Dubai inflows of about INR850-900 crore expected over the next six months, with the bulk in Q2 and Q3 FY27 per management; all proceeds to go to deleveraging.
Associate company inflow of about INR250-258 crore expected.
Management expects external borrowings of about INR700-800 crore (net debt about INR700 crore) at FY26 end, versus about INR1,900 crore currently.
Sugar closing stocks estimated at 5.6 million tonnes (vs 5.3 million tonnes), about two months of consumption; sugar prices expected stable near term.
No monetisation of Goa land (about 260 acres, book value INR163 crore) assumed in plans.
No new ethanol capacity expansion until overcapacity clears; ZEBPL 1,000 KLPD expansion on hold.
capex_capacity: Sugar crushing record 159.7 lakh quintal; capacity utilisation 101.7%, highest ever.
Aira distillery expanded from 100 KLPD to 125 KLPD; FY25 ran 316 days and produced 372 lakh litres of ethanol.
Envien (ZEBPL) 180 KLPD grain-based distillery at Lakhimpur commissioned 1 January 2026, under stabilisation.
Focus shifting to steam, power and chemical consumption reduction; looking for a second UP sugar unit to complement Gobind Sugar Mill at Aira.
Development management strategy is asset-light; no land bank or joint development until about 2-3 years out.
demand_pricing: Ethanol prices stagnant; management expects revision, citing industry representations. OMC bids about 1,800 crore litres against 1,050 crore litres tendered; overcapacity now about 2,000 crore litres.
Government signals on E27, E30, E85 and E100 blending seen as positive for ethanol demand.
Input prices, including chemicals, rose in FY26; macro conditions affecting capex in India and the Middle East.
Real estate DM revenue is a fee on sales value, recognised as phases complete over about 5 years; EBITDA margin on this service revenue cited at 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: How certain is the Dubai inflow this quarter, and how much deleveraging is expected this quarter or next?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said the BCC was received and demand letters are being raised; INR850-900 crore is expected over six months, with the balance of about INR800-850 crore in FY26-27 after retention money.

qa_highlights.question: What will net debt be after these inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatin Jain said external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore less about INR1,200 crore of deleveraging (Dubai plus associate) leaves about INR700 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai project profit and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said Zuari Infraworld's 50% JV share of estimated profit is about INR600 crore on capital invested of INR270-275 crore, giving about INR900 crore of cash back.

qa_highlights.question: What recourse exists if Dubai buyers default?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said RERA in Dubai allows forfeiture of 40% of the apartment value and resale; the timeline could be about a year, but management sees no buyer inquiries or concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the value of strategic investments declined about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Athar Shahab said the holdings are performing operationally and management does not comment on share prices; Texmaco Rail is held as a strategic investment and not consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What drove lower sugar recovery and what can be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Saxena said early-season crushing starting in late October lowered the weighted average recovery; the company ranked fourth of about 14 nearby units and is replacing the 238 variety.

risks_watch: Timing and collection of Dubai inflows (INR850-900 crore) amid West Asia conflict; retention money and buyer defaults could delay them.
Repeated past assurances on deleveraging timing; investor scepticism noted on the call.
Ethanol overcapacity (about 100%) and delayed OMC second and third round tenders affecting Envien ZEBPL utilisation.
Sugar recovery trend lower YoY; input cost inflation including chemicals.
Currency: management says rupee depreciation is favourable for Dubai receivables; forward covers if needed.
Goa land monetisation not factored in; Texmaco Rail provision of about INR700 crore reported by an analyst (not confirmed by management).
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the Dubai cash flows, but guarded on deleveraging timing and evasive on share price and investment value questions. Management repeatedly deferred details (e.g., Texmaco, TIHL project) to other entities.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest ever crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal for the financial year.
So after considering the inflows from the Dubai project of around INR800 crores considering the exchange rate fluctuation and the inflows from our associate company of around INR258 crores.
So we are not presenting a 3 year plan in this call unfortunately.
This amount will be used entirely for deleveraging.

growth.why: Guidance is for deleveraging (net debt ~INR700 crore at FY27 end, backed by INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows and INR250-258 crore associate inflow), not revenue growth; no revenue growth figure given, ethanol expansion is on hold, and sugar utilisation is already at a record 101.7%.
